rows.note: Use the all-purpose colloquial verb 搞 for aimless messing or fidgeting, and for making small adjustments or tinkering.

example.english: Don't fiddle around; concentrate on your revision.

rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for the stringed instrument.

example.english: I learned the fiddle when I was little, and I can still play a few tunes.
example.traditional: 我細個學過小提琴，而家仲識拉幾首歌。
example.jyutping: ngo5 sai3 go3 hok6 gwo3 siu2 tai4 kam4 ji4 gaa1 zung6 sik1 laai1 gei2 sau2 go1

rows.note: Use this for a scam or fraudulent scheme, rather than for an instrument or musician.

example.english: This so-called investment scheme is a fiddle, so do not hand over any money.
example.traditional: 呢個所謂投資計劃根本係騙局，千祈唔好畀錢。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 so2 wai6 tau4 zi1 gai3 waak6 gan1 bun2 hai6 pin3 guk6 cin1 kei4 m4 hou2 bei2 cin2

rows.note: Use 搞手腳 when someone secretly manipulates records, figures, or arrangements to cheat.

example.english: They fiddle the accounts to cheat the company out of a lot of money.

rows.note: Use this specifically for the person who plays the violin in a band.

example.english: As soon as the fiddle player in the band started playing, the whole venue fell silent.
example.traditional: 樂隊個小提琴手一開弓，成個場都靜晒。
example.jyutping: ngok6 deoi2 go3 siu2 tai4 kam4 sau2 jat1 hoi1 gung1 seng4 go3 coeng4 dou1 zing6 saai3

rows.note: Use 拉小提琴 specifically for playing the violin, including a folk or country style.

example.english: The group at the village entrance plays the fiddle every Saturday.
